title: World Golf Village
name: World Golf Village
metaTitle: World Golf Village 1031 Exchange Services in Jacksonville, FL
metaDescription: World Golf Village 1031 exchange coordination for hospitality and office park replacement property near I-95 and St. Augustine.

sections.html:
World Golf Village sits in St. Johns County off I-95 north of St. Augustine, a master-planned development that grew up around the World Golf Hall of Fame and its adjoining convention center, and its replacement-property scope covers a narrower but more specialized band than most Jacksonville-area submarkets: hospitality, office park, and retail product tied to that draw rather than a broad rooftop-driven trade area.

A submittal package for this market should treat the hospitality, office, and retail categories as three separate scopes of work rather than one blended asset class, since financing, franchise, and lease structures differ meaningfully across the three.

sections.heading: Hospitality and Office Park Scope at World Golf Village
sections.html:
The development includes branded-flag hotel product supporting convention and golf-tourism demand, an office park serving both destination-related businesses and the broader St. Johns County commuter base, and a smaller retail component serving both visitors and the surrounding residential growth. Each category carries a distinct lease or franchise structure that should be modeled separately rather than combined into a single blended assumption.

Golf course and clubhouse assets in the immediate vicinity generally trade on a different basis than the hotel and office product, since course-related real estate carries its own maintenance capital schedule and membership-revenue considerations that a standard commercial rent roll does not capture.

sections.heading: Property Types
sections.html:
Replacement candidates at World Golf Village generally fall into the following categories:

  • branded-flag hotels tied to convention and golf-tourism demand
  • multi-tenant office buildings in the surrounding office park
  • single-tenant retail and restaurant pads near the I-95 interchange
  • medical office serving the growing St. Johns County residential base
  • land parcels held for future hospitality or office development

Of these, the office park and medical office categories generally carry the most straightforward underwriting, since they lease on standard commercial terms without the franchise-agreement layer attached to the hospitality product.

sections.heading: I-95/SR 16 Interchange Corridor Specifications
sections.html:
The State Road 16 interchange with I-95 is the operative access point for the entire development, and drive time to that interchange, rather than distance to St. Augustine's historic core, is the more useful underwriting variable for any hospitality or retail property here. St. Johns County has approved substantial residential growth in the surrounding area, driven in part by the county's school district reputation, and that rooftop growth is a slower but steadier demand driver than the convention center's event calendar.

Traffic patterns at the SR 16 interchange shift noticeably during major golf and convention events, and a retail or restaurant tenant's sales data should be reviewed across both event and non-event periods to get an accurate baseline rather than an inflated event-week figure.

sections.heading: Hospitality and Convention-Driven Diligence Items
sections.html:
Any hotel property should be reviewed for its franchise agreement terms separately from the real estate itself, since brand-standard renovation requirements and franchise renewal timing affect the asset independent of the underlying market's performance. Convention center event calendars should be reviewed for booking depth rather than assumed stable, since group and golf-tourism demand can be more cyclical than the office park's commuter-driven occupancy.

Property improvement plan requirements tied to a brand renewal should be quoted from the franchisor directly rather than estimated, since these figures are set by the brand and can represent a material near-term capital obligation that changes the hold-period math for a buyer.

sections.heading: Sequencing With St. Johns County Rooftop Growth
sections.html: Because St. Johns County's broader residential growth is a steadier driver than the convention center's calendar, exchangers looking at World Golf Village should also carry an identification along the SR 16 corridor toward St. Augustine's core as a backup, since that stretch shares the same rooftop-growth logic without the added franchise-agreement complexity of a hotel acquisition. Qualified intermediary and lender coordination should account for the longer diligence period a franchise-agreement review typically requires.

faqs.q: Why should hotel franchise agreements be reviewed separately from the real estate?
faqs.a: Brand-standard renovation requirements and franchise renewal timing affect a hotel asset independent of how the underlying market performs, so a franchise agreement review should be a distinct diligence step from the standard property condition report.

faqs.q: Is convention center demand a stable underwriting basis at World Golf Village?
faqs.a: It should be treated cautiously. Group and golf-tourism event bookings can be more cyclical than the office park's commuter-driven occupancy, so event calendars should be reviewed for actual booking depth rather than assumed stable, and a buyer should ask for at least three prior years of booking data rather than a single strong year.

faqs.q: What is driving longer-term demand at World Golf Village beyond the convention center?
faqs.a: St. Johns County's residential growth, supported in part by the county's school district reputation, is a steadier driver than the convention center's event calendar and supports the office park and retail categories as well.

faqs.q: What backup submarket pairs with World Golf Village?
faqs.a: The SR 16 corridor toward St. Augustine's core shares the same rooftop-growth logic without the added franchise-agreement complexity of a hotel acquisition, making it a practical backup identification for buyers who want to avoid the hospitality diligence layer altogether.

faqs.q: Why does the I-95/SR 16 interchange matter more than distance to St. Augustine?
faqs.a: Drive time to the interchange is the more useful variable for hospitality and retail underwriting here, since visitor and commuter traffic routes through that access point rather than through the historic core, and a property's practical accessibility should be measured from the interchange rather than from a straight-line map distance.
